title.zh: 卷三百〇八 列傳第六十七 上官正 盧斌 周審玉 裴濟 李繼宣 張旦 張煦 張佶
title.en: Volume 308 Biographies 67: Shang Guanzheng, Lu Bin, Zhou Shenyu, Pei Ji, Li Jixuan, Zhang Dan, Zhang Xu, Zhang Ji
title.raw: 卷三百〇八 列傳第六十七 上官正 盧斌 周審玉 裴濟 李繼宣 張旦 張煦 張佶 Volume 308 Biographies 67: Shang Guanzheng, Lu Bin, Zhou Shenyu, Pei Ji, Li Jixuan, Zhang Dan, Zhang Xu, Zhang Ji

sentences.zh: 上官正

translations.literal: Shang Guanzheng
translations.idiomatic: Shang Guanzheng

sentences.zh: 上官正，字常清，開封人。

translations.literal: Shang Guanzheng, courtesy name Changqing, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Guanzheng, whose courtesy name was Changqing, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少舉《三傳》，後為鄜州攝官。

translations.literal: In his youth he passed the examinations in the Three Commentaries; later he served as acting official in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he passed the examinations in the Three Commentaries; he later served as an acting official in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，召授殿前承旨，屢遣鞫獄，遷供奉官、閤門祗候、天雄監軍。

translations.literal: During the Yongxi era he was summoned and appointed Palace Front Commissioner; he was repeatedly sent to investigate cases, and was promoted to Presentation Officer, Gate Attendant, and Supervisory Commissioner at Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi reign he was called to court and made Palace Front Commissioner. Sent repeatedly to try criminal cases, he rose to Presentation Officer, Gate Attendant, and military supervisor at Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，轉作坊副使、劍門都監。

translations.literal: During the Chunhua era he was transferred to Deputy Commissioner of the Workshops and Superintendent of Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunhua period he became Deputy Commissioner of the Workshops and superintendent of Jianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 李順之亂，分其黨趨劍門，時疲兵數百人，正奮勵士氣以禦之。

translations.literal: When Li Shun rebelled, a division of his followers advanced on Jianmen; at the time there were only a few hundred weary troops, but Zheng roused their morale to resist.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Shun's rebellion, part of his force marched on Jianmen Pass. Zheng had only a few hundred exhausted soldiers, yet he stirred their spirits and held the pass.

sentences.zh: 會成都監軍宿翰領兵投劍門，與正兵合，因迎擊，大破賊數千眾，斬馘殆盡。

translations.literal: It happened that Su Han, the supervisory commissioner at Chengdu, led troops to Jianmen and joined Zheng's force; they met the enemy in attack and utterly routed several thousand rebels, killing nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Su Han, the army supervisor at Chengdu, then brought his troops to Jianmen and united with Zheng. They counterattacked and smashed a rebel force of several thousand, slaughtering almost the entire host.

sentences.zh: 奏至，太宗嘉之，詔書獎飭，並賜襲衣、金帶，超正為六宅使、劍州刺史、充劍門部署，翰自供奉官擢崇儀使、領昭州刺史。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Taizong commended them; an edict praised and admonished them, and bestowed court robes and gold belts. Zheng was promoted beyond regular rank to Commissioner of the Six Residences, Prefect of Jianzhou, and deployed at Jianmen; Han was raised from Presentation Officer to Commissioner of Ceremonial Rites and given charge of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court, Emperor Taizong praised them both. An edict commended their service and rewarded them with court robes and gold belts. Zheng was promoted out of turn to Commissioner of the Six Residences, made prefect of Jianzhou, and placed in command at Jianmen; Han was raised from Presentation Officer to Commissioner of Ceremonial Rites and appointed prefect of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 數月，正被疾，請尋醫，至闕。

translations.literal: Several months later Zheng fell ill, requested leave to seek medical treatment, and came to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later Zheng fell ill and asked permission to seek treatment at court.

sentences.zh: 疾愈，入對，上勞問久之，復遣還任所，賜以金丹、良藥、衣帶、白金千兩、馬三匹，授以方略，令招撫殘孽，慰勉遣之。

translations.literal: When his illness was cured he was received in audience; the emperor questioned and comforted him at length, then sent him back to his post, bestowing elixir pills, fine medicines, robes and belts, a thousand taels of silver, and three horses, and giving him a plan to win over the remaining rebels, with words of encouragement as he dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: After he recovered he was received in audience. The emperor questioned him at length and sent him back to his post, granting elixir pills, fine medicines, robes, a belt, a thousand taels of silver, and three horses. He also gave him a strategy for winning over the remaining rebels and dismissed him with words of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 初，川賊甚盛，朝議深以棧路為憂，正以孤軍力戰挫賊鋒，自是閣道無壅，王師得以長驅而入。

translations.literal: At first the rebels in Sichuan were very strong, and the court was deeply worried about the plank-road route; Zheng, fighting alone with his army, blunted the rebels' momentum, and from then on the gallery roads were unobstructed, so the imperial army could advance at full speed.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Sichuan rebels were formidable, and the court feared greatly for the plank-road supply line. Zheng fought on alone and blunted their advance, after which the mountain passes lay open and the imperial army could drive deep into the province.

sentences.zh: 賊眾三百餘，敗歸成都，順怒其驚眾，盡斬之，然自此沮氣矣。

translations.literal: More than three hundred rebels returned defeated to Chengdu; Shun, angry that they had alarmed the army, executed them all, but from that time their morale was broken.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred defeated rebels fled back to Chengdu. Li Shun, furious that they had spread panic in his ranks, had them all executed, and from that moment his followers lost heart.

sentences.zh: 後賊既誅，餘寇匿山谷，恃險結集，剽劫為患。

translations.literal: After the rebels were executed, the remaining bandits hid in mountain valleys, relying on difficult terrain to gather and raid as a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: After the main rebels were destroyed, remnants hid in the mountains, rallied in defensible terrain, and plagued the countryside with raids.

sentences.zh: 王繼恩百計召誘不至，正諭以朝廷恩信，皆相率出降。

translations.literal: Wang Jien used every stratagem to summon and entice them but they would not come; Zheng instructed them in the court's grace and good faith, and they all came out in succession to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jien tried every means to lure them out, without success. Zheng appealed to them with the court's grace and trustworthiness, and they came out to surrender one after another.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加峰州團練使，與雷有終並為西川招安使，代王繼恩。

translations.literal: Before long he was given the additional title of Militia Commissioner of Fengzhou, and together with Lei Youzhong served as Pacification Commissioner of Western Sichuan, replacing Wang Jien.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Militia Commissioner of Fengzhou and, together with Lei Youzhong, appointed Pacification Commissioner of Western Sichuan in Wang Jien's place.

sentences.zh: 正木強好淩人，自謂平賊有勞，受人主知，無所顧忌。

translations.literal: Zheng was obstinate and fond of domineering others; he considered himself meritorious for pacifying the rebels and favored by the sovereign, and was without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was stubborn and overbearing. He believed his service in suppressing the rebellion had won him the emperor's favor, and he acted without restraint.

sentences.zh: 數面攻兩川官吏之短而暴揚之，眾積怨怒，多上章訴其不法者。

translations.literal: He repeatedly attacked the faults of officials in the two Sichuan circuits to their faces and publicly exposed them; the masses accumulated resentment and anger, and many submitted memorials accusing him of illegal conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly confronted officials of the two Sichuan circuits with their faults and exposed them publicly. Resentment mounted, and many submitted memorials accusing him of misconduct.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂近臣曰：「人臣可任用者，朕常欲保全。

translations.literal: Taizong said to his close ministers: "For ministers who can be employed, I always wish to preserve them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong told his close advisers, "When I find a minister I can use, I always try to protect him.

sentences.zh: 正婞直而失於謙和，每謗書至，朕雖力與明辯，然眾怒難犯，恐其不能自全。

translations.literal: Zheng is upright but lacking in humility and harmony; whenever a slanderous memorial arrives, although I strive to clarify matters for him, yet the wrath of the multitude is hard to withstand, and I fear he may not be able to preserve himself."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng is upright but lacks humility. Each time a denunciation reaches me I do my best to defend him, yet popular anger is not easily defied, and I fear he may not be able to save himself."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜手劄戒諭曰：「言者，君子之樞機，樞機之發，榮辱之主，不可不慎也。

translations.literal: " He then bestowed a personal letter of admonition, saying: "Speech is the pivot of the gentleman; when the pivot moves, honor and disgrace follow—one cannot be careless.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent a personal letter of admonition: "Speech is the pivot on which a gentleman turns; when that pivot moves, honor and disgrace follow. You must be careful.

sentences.zh: 夫遇事輒發，悔不可及。

translations.literal: To speak out on every matter as it arises—regret cannot overtake it.
translations.idiomatic: To speak out on every passing matter is to invite regret that cannot be undone.

sentences.zh: 儻自恃無瑕，而好面攻人之短，豈謂喜怒不形於色耶？

translations.literal: If you rely on your own spotlessness and delight in attacking others' faults to their faces, can this be called keeping joy and anger from showing in one's countenance?
translations.idiomatic: If you trust in your own blamelessness and delight in confronting others with their faults, is that what it means to keep joy and anger from showing on one's face?

sentences.zh: 當以和輯遠民為念，斯盡善矣。

translations.literal: You should keep in mind harmonizing and gathering the distant people—then all will be well."
translations.idiomatic: Keep in mind the need to win over and reassure the people of the frontier regions; that will be best of all."

sentences.zh: 」正上表謝。

translations.literal: " Zheng submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，改莊宅使。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he was changed to Commissioner of Imperial Estates.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong came to the throne, Zheng was made Commissioner of Imperial Estates.

sentences.zh: 是秋，廣武叛卒劉於嘯聚數千輩，逐都巡檢使韓景祐，略漢蜀邛州、懷安永康軍。

translations.literal: That autumn, the rebel soldier Liu Yu of Guangwu gathered several thousand followers, drove out the Chief Inspector Han Jingyou, and plundered Qiongzhou, Huai'an, and Yongkang Army in Han-Shu.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Liu Yu, a mutineer from Guangwu, rallied several thousand men, expelled Chief Inspector Han Jingyou, and overran Qiongzhou, Huai'an, and Yongkang Army in the Han-Shu region.

sentences.zh: 正與鈐轄馬知節領兵趨新津，抵方井，擊敗之，斬於，平其黨。

translations.literal: Zheng together with Commissioner Ma Zhijie led troops to Xinjin, reached Fangjing, defeated them, beheaded Yu, and pacified his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng and Commissioner Ma Zhijie led troops to Xinjin, reached Fangjing, routed the rebels, beheaded Liu Yu, and crushed his followers.

sentences.zh: 遷南作坊使，賜錦袍、金帶。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Southern Workshops and bestowed a brocade robe and gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commissioner of the Southern Workshops and rewarded with a brocade robe and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，召還，擢拜東上閤門使、勾當軍頭引見司，俄權戶部使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was recalled, promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and put in charge of the Army Head Reception Office; shortly thereafter he acted as Commissioner of the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping reign he was recalled and promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner, placed in charge of the Army Head Reception Office, and soon made acting Commissioner of the Household Bureau.

sentences.zh: 二年，出知滄州，徙高陽關副都部署，真拜洺州團練使。

translations.literal: In the second year he went out as prefect of Cangzhou, was moved to Deputy Commander at Gaoyang Pass, and was formally appointed Militia Commissioner of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was sent out as prefect of Cangzhou, transferred to deputy commander at Gaoyang Pass, and formally appointed Militia Commissioner of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，以為行營先鋒鈐轄。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured the north, he was made Vanguard Commissioner of the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the north, he was made vanguard commissioner of the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋知青州，未行，會王均叛蜀，命為峽路都鈐轄，移知梓州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made prefect of Qingzhou; before he departed, Wang Jun rebelled in Shu, and he was ordered to be Chief Commissioner of the Gorges Route and transferred to prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed prefect of Qingzhou, but before he could take up the post Wang Jun rebelled in Shu. He was made Chief Commissioner of the Gorges Route and transferred to prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 又歷滄、瀛、鎮、貝四州，高陽關部署。

translations.literal: He also served in succession at the four prefectures of Cang, Ying, Zhen, and Bei, and as Commander at Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as prefect of Cang, Ying, Zhen, and Bei, and as commander at Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 以足疾，求知磁州，手詔慰勉。

translations.literal: Because of illness in his feet he requested appointment to Cizhou; an imperial letter in the emperor's own hand comforted and encouraged him.
translations.idiomatic: Afflicted with foot trouble, he asked to be sent to Cizhou. The emperor answered with a personal letter of encouragement.

sentences.zh: 會邢州地震，民居不安，徙正典之。

translations.literal: It happened that Xingzhou suffered an earthquake and the people's dwellings were unsettled; Zheng was transferred to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: When an earthquake unsettled the people of Xingzhou, Zheng was transferred there to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 移潞州。

translations.literal: He was moved to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 景德中，以河北新經兵革，慎擇守臣，以正知貝州，遷洺州防禦使，復知滄州，移同州。

translations.literal: During the Jingde era, because Hebei had recently undergone warfare, guard officials were chosen with care; Zheng was made prefect of Beizhou, promoted to Defender of Mingzhou, again made prefect of Cangzhou, and moved to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde reign, with Hebei still recovering from war, the court chose its frontier governors carefully. Zheng was made prefect of Beizhou, promoted to Defender of Mingzhou, returned to Cangzhou, and then sent to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 再表引年，授左龍武軍大將軍、平州防禦使，分司西京。

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial citing his years and was appointed General of the Left Dragon Martial Army and Defender of Pingzhou, with duties at the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned again to retire on account of age and was made General of the Left Dragon Martial Army and Defender of Pingzhou, with duties at the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官致仕，賜全俸，仍以見緡給之。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he retired with his existing rank, was granted full salary, and still received cash payments in addition.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired at his existing rank, was granted full salary, and continued to receive cash stipends as well.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died, at the age of seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 子璨至內殿崇班。

translations.literal: His son Can rose to Inner Hall Attendant of the Honored Class.
translations.idiomatic: His son Can rose to Inner Hall Attendant of the Honored Class.

sentences.zh: 端拱中，又為永舉軍、華州巡檢。

translations.literal: During the Duangong era he again served as Inspector of Yongju Army and Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Duangong reign he again served as inspector of Yongju Army and Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 時大賊侯和尚、劉渥劫興平、櫟陽，殺捕賊官二人。

translations.literal: At the time the great bandits Hou Heshang and Liu Wo raided Xingping and Liyang and killed two bandit-suppression officers.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the major bandits Hou Heshang and Liu Wo raided Xingping and Liyang and killed two officers charged with suppressing banditry.

sentences.zh: 斌率兵掩襲，且追且鬥，薄南山，渡渭水，抵鳳翔，復至耀州，擒斬並盡。

translations.literal: Bin led troops in a surprise attack, pursuing and fighting as he went, pressing to South Mountain, crossing the Wei River, reaching Fengxiang, then coming again to Yaozhou, capturing and beheading them all.
translations.idiomatic: Bin led a surprise attack, fighting as he pursued the bandits to South Mountain, crossed the Wei River, reached Fengxiang, then pressed on to Yaozhou and captured and killed them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 以勞，改供奉官。

translations.literal: For his labor he was changed to Presentation Officer.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to Presentation Officer.

sentences.zh: 召還，面加獎慰，授閤門祗候，又賜白金、緡錢、衣帶。

translations.literal: He was recalled and personally commended and comforted, appointed Gate Attendant, and again bestowed silver, cash, and robes with belt.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was commended in person and made Gate Attendant. He was also given silver, cash, and robes with a belt.

sentences.zh: 尋為梓、遂十二州都巡檢使，太宗諭之曰：「川陝人情易搖，設有寇攘，雖他境亦當襲逐，仍許便宜從事，不須中覆。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Chief Inspector of the twelve prefectures of Zi and Sui; Taizong instructed him: "The people of Sichuan and Shaanxi are easily unsettled; if there is banditry, even in another jurisdiction you should pursue and drive them off, and you are permitted to act at discretion without reporting to the center."
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Chief Inspector of the twelve prefectures of Zi and Sui. Taizong told him, "The people of Sichuan and Shaanxi are easily stirred up. If bandits appear, pursue them even beyond your jurisdiction, and act at your own discretion without waiting for approval from court."

sentences.zh: 」淳化二年，賊任誘等寇昌、合州。

translations.literal: " In the second year of Chunhua the bandits Ren You and others raided Chang and He prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua the bandits Ren You and others raided Chang and He prefectures.

sentences.zh: 斌率兵頓昌州南牛鬥山，偵知賊在龍水鎮，值大雨，斌馳馬四十里，騎從數十人，遂斬誘等百餘級，賊眾悉平。

translations.literal: Bin led troops and encamped at Ox-Fight Mountain south of Changzhou; scouts learned the bandits were at Longshui Town. A heavy rain fell; Bin galloped forty li with several dozen horsemen, and thereupon beheaded more than a hundred of You and the rest; the bandit host was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bin encamped his troops at Ox-Fight Mountain south of Changzhou. Scouts reported that the bandits were at Longshui Town. Despite heavy rain, Bin galloped forty li with only a few dozen horsemen, killed more than a hundred men including Ren You, and crushed the entire band.

sentences.zh: 三年，富順監蠻掠榮州，斌晨夜倍道以赴，得州兵千人，署隨軍糧料以張其勢。

translations.literal: In the third year the barbarians of Fushun Supervisorate raided Rongzhou; Bin traveled day and night by forced marches to go to its aid, obtained a thousand prefectural troops, and appointed an army provisioner to magnify his force.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the tribes of Fushun Supervisorate raided Rongzhou. Bin marched day and night at forced pace, gathered a thousand local troops, and appointed an army provisioner to strengthen his position.

sentences.zh: 蠻乃遁，追至地頭鎮東南八十里，樹柵，招其酋甫羌一阿奴綱，諭以朝旨，歃血刻石為盟而遣之。

translations.literal: The barbarians then fled; he pursued them eighty li southeast of Ditou Town, erected palisades, summoned their chieftain Fuqiang Yi Anu Gang, instructed him in the court's decree, and sent him away after a blood-oath alliance carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: The tribesmen fled. Bin pursued them eighty li southeast of Ditou Town, built a stockade, and summoned their chieftain Fuqiang Yi Anu Gang. After instructing him in the court's decree, he sent him away with a blood-oath alliance recorded on stone.

sentences.zh: 俄而榮、戎、資州、富順監賊十五隊鈔鄉邑，斌擒三百人，部送闕下，餘悉臨敵斬戮。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter fifteen bands of bandits from Rong, Rong, Zi, and Fushun Supervisorate raided the countryside; Bin captured three hundred men and escorted them to the capital, while the rest he beheaded in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon fifteen rebel bands from Rong, Rong, Zi, and Fushun Supervisorate were raiding the countryside. Bin captured three hundred men and sent them to court; the rest he killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 四年，賊王盡復起榮、資，斌擊滅之，盡縛以獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the bandit Wang Jin again rose in Rong and Zi; Bin attacked and destroyed him, binding him entirely and presenting him as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the bandit Wang Jin rebelled again in Rong and Zi. Bin destroyed him, bound him, and sent him to court as a captive.

sentences.zh: 遷內殿崇班。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Inner Hall Attendant of the Honored Class.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Inner Hall Attendant of the Honored Class.

sentences.zh: 是冬，李順為亂，斌即率兵六百抵成都，鬥戰連月，殺數萬人。

translations.literal: That winter Li Shun rebelled; Bin immediately led six hundred troops to Chengdu, fought for months, and killed tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, when Li Shun rebelled, Bin led six hundred men straight to Chengdu and fought for months, killing tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 明年，成都不守，斌還梓州，集十州兵赴援，知州張雍委以監護之任。

translations.literal: The next year Chengdu could not be held; Bin returned to Zizhou, gathered troops from ten prefectures to go to the rescue, and Prefect Zhang Yong entrusted him with supervisory duties.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when Chengdu fell, Bin withdrew to Zizhou, rallied troops from ten prefectures, and was entrusted by Prefect Zhang Yong with command of the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 會江水泛溢，毀子城。

translations.literal: It happened that the river waters overflowed and destroyed the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: The river then flooded and destroyed the inner city.

sentences.zh: 斌勸諭州民，翌日，畚鍤大集，自城西大濠中掘塹深丈，決西河水，注之以環城。

translations.literal: Bin exhorted and instructed the people of the prefecture; the next day shovels and picks gathered in great numbers, and from the great moat west of the city they dug a trench a zhang deep, broke the western river, and poured it in to encircle the city.
translations.idiomatic: Bin rallied the townspeople. The next day laborers gathered in force, dug a trench a zhang deep from the great moat west of the city, diverted the western river, and flooded the ground around the walls.

sentences.zh: 二月，賊渠相里貴眾二十一萬傅城下，城中兵裁三千。

translations.literal: In the second month the bandit leader Xiangli Gui with a host of two hundred ten thousand pressed against the city; troops within the city numbered only three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the rebel leader Xiangli Gui brought two hundred ten thousand men against the walls, while the garrison had only three thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 斌曰：「軍法倍兵不戰，然狂醜烏合，非訓練之師，以吾仗天子威靈，必可殲蕩。

translations.literal: Bin said: "By military law one does not fight when the enemy is twice one's strength; yet these mad and ugly rabble gathered without discipline are no trained army—relying on the Son of Heaven's majesty, we can surely destroy them."
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "Military law forbids fighting when the enemy outnumbers you two to one, but this rabble is undisciplined and wild. With the Son of Heaven's authority behind us, we can surely crush them."

sentences.zh: 」即感厲士伍，負土塞南北門，為固守之計。

translations.literal: " He immediately inspired and urged the soldiers, had them carry earth to block the north and south gates, and made plans for a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: He roused his men, had them carry earth to block the north and south gates, and prepared for a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 又突出與賊戰，擊刺三十餘合，賊稍卻。

translations.literal: He again sallied forth to fight the bandits, thrusting and stabbing through more than thirty encounters, and the bandits gradually fell back.
translations.idiomatic: He then led a sortie and fought more than thirty rounds of close combat before the rebels began to fall back.

sentences.zh: 俄復大設機石、連弩、衝車、雲梯，四面鼓噪乘城，矢石亂下，斌與州將隨機設備。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter they again set up in great numbers catapults, repeating crossbows, battering rams, and scaling ladders; on all four sides they beat drums and clamored as they mounted the walls, arrows and stones raining down chaotically; Bin and the prefectural generals improvised defenses as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon brought up catapults, repeating crossbows, battering rams, and scaling ladders, attacked from all sides with drums and war cries, and rained arrows and stones on the walls. Bin and the local commanders improvised their defenses as the situation demanded.

sentences.zh: 長圍八十日，會王繼恩令石知顒率兵來援，斌出東門迎勞王師，賊不戰而潰。

translations.literal: The long siege lasted eighty days; it happened that Wang Jien ordered Shi Zhiyong to lead troops to the rescue; Bin went out the east gate to welcome and comfort the imperial army, and the bandits collapsed without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted eighty days. Wang Jien then sent Shi Zhiyong with reinforcements. Bin went out the east gate to welcome the imperial troops, and the rebels broke without a fight.

sentences.zh: 斌乘勝追斬及納降二萬餘。

translations.literal: Bin pursued in victory, beheading and accepting the surrender of more than twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Bin pressed the advantage, killing rebels and accepting the surrender of more than twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 五月，賊數萬圍閬州，斌領千兵赴之，斬首五千，圍遂解。

translations.literal: In the fifth month several tens of thousands of bandits besieged Langzhou; Bin led a thousand troops to go to its aid, beheaded five thousand, and the siege was thereupon lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month tens of thousands of rebels besieged Langzhou. Bin marched with a thousand men, killed five thousand, and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 又至蓬州老鴉山，賊眾三千為陣拒斌，斌擊敗之，至城下，賊復大集，斬三千級。

translations.literal: He again went to Old Crow Mountain in Pengzhou; three thousand bandits formed a battle line to resist Bin; Bin defeated them, reached the foot of the city, the bandits gathered again in force, and he beheaded three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Old Crow Mountain in Pengzhou, where three thousand rebels formed a line to block him. Bin defeated them, pursued to the city walls, and when the enemy rallied again he killed three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 蓬州平，斌傳詔安撫蓬、閬、渠、達四州，擢授西京作坊使，領成州刺史。

translations.literal: When Pengzhou was pacified, Bin transmitted the edict to pacify and reassure the four prefectures of Peng, Lang, Qu, and Da, was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops, and given charge of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Pengzhou was pacified, Bin carried out an edict to reassure the four prefectures of Peng, Lang, Qu, and Da. He was promoted to Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops and made prefect of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 斌在川峽六年，以孤軍禦寇，累立戰功，表求入奏。

translations.literal: Bin was in the Sichuan gorges for six years, defending against bandits with a lone army and repeatedly establishing battle merit; he submitted a memorial requesting audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: Bin spent six years in the Sichuan gorges fighting bandits with isolated forces and winning repeated victories. He petitioned to report in person at court.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣使諭之曰：「俟妖孽盡殄，當召汝。

translations.literal: Taizong sent an envoy to instruct him: "Wait until the evil brood is entirely exterminated, then I shall summon you."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sent word: "When the rebels are utterly destroyed, I shall summon you."

sentences.zh: 」既而賊黨集梓、綿、漢三州境上，斌往平之。

translations.literal: " Shortly thereafter bandit factions gathered on the borders of the three prefectures of Zi, Mian, and Han; Bin went to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebel bands gathered on the borders of Zi, Mian, and Han, and Bin went to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，代還，太宗親加勞問。

translations.literal: Before long he was replaced and returned; Taizong personally questioned and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was relieved and recalled. Taizong received him in person and praised his service.

sentences.zh: 拜東上閤門使、檢校左僕射，加食邑三百戶，賜白金千兩、袍笏、金帶。

translations.literal: He was appointed Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, with three hundred additional households in his fief, and bestowed a thousand taels of silver, robes and court tablet, and a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner and Acting Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, granted three hundred additional households in his fief, and rewarded with a thousand taels of silver, court robes, a tablet, and a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 上言：「葭萌路出師討賊，可直入利州。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "If troops march out by the Jiameng route to attack bandits, they can enter Lizhou directly.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "If troops march against rebels by the Jiameng route, they can enter Lizhou directly.

sentences.zh: 若寇焚棧道，劍門之險不足固也，請置砦柵。

translations.literal: If the enemy burns the plank road, the peril of Jianmen will not be secure enough; I request that stockades and palisades be established."
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy burns the plank road, Jianmen Pass alone will not hold. I ask that stockades and palisades be built along the route."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved his request.

sentences.zh: 尋命為銀、夏兵馬鈐轄，遣與李繼隆等五路出師討李繼遷。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to be Military Commissioner of Yin and Xia, and sent with Li Jilong and others on five routes to campaign against Li Jiqian.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Military Commissioner of Yin and Xia and sent with Li Jilong and others on five columns to campaign against Li Jiqian.

sentences.zh: 斌求對，懇言曰：「羌夷之族，馬驕兵悍，往來無定，敗則走他境，疾戰沙漠，非天兵所利。

translations.literal: Bin requested audience and earnestly said: "The Qiang and Yi peoples have proud horses and fierce soldiers; they come and go without fixed pattern; when defeated they flee to other regions; swift battle in the desert is not advantageous to the heavenly army.
translations.idiomatic: Bin sought an audience and urged earnestly, "The Qiang and tribal peoples ride swift horses and fight fiercely. They move without pattern, and when defeated flee into other territories. Rapid battle in the desert does not favor the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 不若堅保靈州，於內地多積芻糧，以師援送。

translations.literal: It would be better to hold Lingzhou firmly, store much fodder and grain in the interior, and send relief forces to support it.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to hold Lingzhou firmly, stockpile fodder and grain in the interior, and send relief columns to sustain it.

sentences.zh: 苟其至也，會兵首尾擊之，庶幾無枉費，而不失固圉之策矣。

translations.literal: If they arrive, unite forces to strike them head and tail; then perhaps there will be no wasted effort and the strategy of securing the frontier will not be lost."
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy comes, strike them from front and rear with combined forces. That way effort will not be wasted and the frontier will still be secured."

sentences.zh: 」時業已出師，不從其議。

translations.literal: " At the time the army had already marched out, and his proposal was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: By then the army had already marched, and the court did not accept his advice.

sentences.zh: 改授靈環路鈐轄，領兵二萬為前鋒，令於烏、白池與諸軍會。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Commissioner of the Ling-Huan Circuit, leading twenty thousand troops as vanguard, ordered to join the other armies at the Black and White Pools.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Commissioner of the Ling-Huan Circuit, given twenty thousand men as vanguard, and ordered to join the other armies at the Black and White Pools.

sentences.zh: 斌謂李繼隆曰：「靈州抵烏、白池，月餘方至。

translations.literal: Bin said to Li Jilong: "From Lingzhou to the Black and White Pools is more than a month on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Bin told Li Jilong, "From Lingzhou to the Black and White Pools takes more than a month.

sentences.zh: 若自環州橐駝路，裁十日程。

translations.literal: If one goes by the camel route from Huanzhou, it is only ten days' journey."
translations.idiomatic: By the camel route from Huanzhou it is only ten days."

sentences.zh: 」即不俟詔而往，與諸將失期，不見賊而還。

translations.literal: " He thereupon went without awaiting the edict, missed the rendezvous with the other generals, saw no enemy, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Without waiting for orders he set out, missed the rendezvous with the other commanders, found no enemy, and returned.

sentences.zh: 俄徙屯寧州，以疾召歸，勾當軍頭引見司。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was moved to garrison at Ningzhou; because of illness he was recalled and put in charge of the Army Head Reception Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to garrison Ningzhou, then recalled on account of illness and placed in charge of the Army Head Reception Office.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，卒，年五十。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he died, at the age of fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping reign he died at the age of fifty.

sentences.zh: 子文質殿中丞。

translations.literal: His son Wenzhi became Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wenzhi became Palace Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 周審玉

translations.literal: Zhou Shenyu
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shenyu

sentences.zh: 周審玉，開封人。

translations.literal: Zhou Shenyu was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shenyu came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父勳，以親校事唐明宗，累立戰功，太平興國中，至隰州團練使。

translations.literal: His father Xun, as a personal guard serving Emperor Mingzong of Tang, repeatedly established battle merit; during Taiping Xingguo he rose to Militia Commissioner of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xun had served Emperor Mingzong of Tang as a personal guard, won repeated victories in battle, and during Taiping Xingguo rose to Militia Commissioner of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，審玉蔭補殿直，從世宗平瓦橋關，甚見親信。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande of Zhou, Shenyu entered service by hereditary privilege as Palace Attendant, followed Shizong in pacifying Waqiao Pass, and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhou Xiande reign, Shenyu entered service by hereditary privilege as Palace Attendant, followed Emperor Shizong in pacifying Waqiao Pass, and won his close trust.

sentences.zh: 太祖受禪，為供奉官，未幾，加閤門祗候。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the abdication he became Presentation Officer; before long he was made Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Shenyu became Presentation Officer and soon Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 累遷崇儀、洛苑副使，西京作坊使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Ceremonial Rites Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner of the Luoyang Park, and Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to Ceremonial Rites Commissioner, Deputy Commissioner of the Luoyang Park, and Commissioner of the Western Capital Workshops.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，契丹犯塞，潘美屯師定州，審玉為監軍。

translations.literal: During Yongxi the Khitan violated the frontier; Pan Mei stationed troops at Dingzhou, and Shenyu served as supervisory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi reign, when the Khitan raided the frontier, Pan Mei stationed his army at Dingzhou and Shenyu served as army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 嘗與敵戰，而先鋒劉緒陷賊，審玉躍馬趣擊，拔緒而還，以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: He once fought the enemy, and when the vanguard Liu Xu was trapped by the bandits, Shenyu leaped on his horse and rushed to attack, rescued Xu and returned, and became known for bravery.
translations.idiomatic: In one battle the vanguard Liu Xu was trapped by the enemy. Shenyu spurred his horse forward, rescued Xu, and became renowned for his courage.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，知貝州。

translations.literal: During Chunhua he was made prefect of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua reign he was made prefect of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 有驍捷卒戍州者三十七人，同謀殺審玉，劫庫兵而叛，推虞候趙咸雍為首。

translations.literal: Thirty-seven Swift-and-Bold soldiers garrisoning the prefecture conspired together to kill Shenyu, seize weapons from the arsenal and rebel, and made the Assistant Commander Zhao Xianyong their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-seven Swift-and-Bold soldiers garrisoned at the prefecture plotted to kill Shenyu, seize arms from the arsenal, and rebel, making Assistant Commander Zhao Xianyong their leader.

sentences.zh: 審玉覺之，與轉運使王嗣宗率兵悉擒其黨，斬十五級，磔咸雍於市。

translations.literal: Shenyu detected it; together with Transport Commissioner Wang Sizong he led troops and captured all their faction, beheaded fifteen, and dismembered Xianyong in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyu discovered the plot. With Transport Commissioner Wang Sizong he led troops, captured the entire conspiracy, executed fifteen men, and dismembered Xianyong in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 先是，咸雍父鏻，晉天福中，嘗誘契丹屠州城。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xianyong's father Lin, during Tianfu of Jin, had once induced the Khitan to slaughter the people of the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xianyong's father Lin had, during the Jin Tianfu era, induced the Khitan to massacre the people of the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 至是五十年，而其子戮於都市，舊老猶記其事，咸異之。

translations.literal: At this time fifty years had passed, yet his son was executed in the capital; old men still remembered the affair, and all regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty years had passed, yet now the son was executed in the capital. Old residents still remembered what his father had done, and everyone found the turn of fate remarkable.

sentences.zh: 審玉以功領順州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit Shenyu was given charge of Shunzhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made prefect of Shunzhou.

sentences.zh: 至道初，徙幷州鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhidao he was transferred to Commissioner of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhidao reign he was transferred to Commissioner of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，知鳳翔府。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he was made administrator of Fengxiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping reign he was made administrator of Fengxiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有桑門乘傳而西，以市木為名，威動府縣。

translations.literal: A Buddhist monk traveled west on imperial relay horses, using the purchase of timber as his pretext, and his authority shook the prefecture and counties.
translations.idiomatic: A Buddhist monk traveled west on imperial relay horses, claiming to be buying timber, and his authority intimidated prefectural and county officials.

sentences.zh: 審玉曰：「此有所倚而為也。

translations.literal: Shenyu said: "This man acts with someone backing him."
translations.idiomatic: Shenyu said, "He must have powerful backing behind him."

sentences.zh: 」因按詰之，盡得其奸狀，杖其背，械送闕下。

translations.literal: " He thereupon investigated and interrogated him, fully obtained evidence of his wicked conduct, flogged his back, and sent him in fetters to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He investigated and interrogated the monk, uncovered the full extent of his misconduct, had him flogged, and sent him to court in chains.

sentences.zh: 以目疾，代還，奉朝請，俄丁內艱。

translations.literal: Because of eye disease he was replaced and recalled, served as Court Attendant, and shortly thereafter mourned his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Afflicted with eye trouble, he was relieved and recalled to serve as Court Attendant, and soon afterward went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 既而謂親友曰：「僕齒髮遲暮，而未能辭祿仕者，良以慰母心爾，今可行其志矣。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he said to relatives and friends: "I am already old in teeth and hair, yet have been unable to resign my salary and office—this was only to comfort my mother's heart; now I may carry out my wish."
translations.idiomatic: He later told relatives and friends, "I am already old, yet I have stayed in office only to comfort my mother. Now I may do as I wish."

sentences.zh: 」乃拜章請老，得千牛衛大將軍致仕。

translations.literal: " He thereupon submitted a memorial requesting retirement and was granted retirement as General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting retirement and was granted retirement as General of the Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 審玉晚年，好讀《神農本草》，留意方術。

translations.literal: In his later years Shenyu delighted in reading the Divine Farmer's Materia Medica and paid attention to medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Shenyu delighted in reading the Divine Farmer's Materia Medica and took an interest in medicine.

sentences.zh: 少長兵間，習知攻守之法。

translations.literal: From youth he grew up amid armies and was practiced in methods of attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from youth amid armies, he was well versed in attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗召至便坐，示以攻戰器。

translations.literal: Zhenzong once summoned him to the informal seat and showed him weapons of attack and battle.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong once summoned him to an informal audience and showed him weapons of war.

sentences.zh: 方奏對，疾作，詔遣使就第，賜白金慰恤之。

translations.literal: Just as he was responding in audience his illness came on; an edict sent an envoy to his residence and bestowed silver to comfort and relieve him.
translations.idiomatic: While he was answering at audience his illness struck. The emperor sent an envoy to his home and granted silver to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 子允迪，為虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Yundi became Outer Gentleman of the Works Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yundi became Outer Gentleman of the Works Bureau.

sentences.zh: 太平興國末，江表盜起，命為巡檢，遷崇儀副使。

translations.literal: At the end of Taiping Xingguo bandits rose in the lands south of the Yangzi; he was ordered to serve as Inspector and was promoted to Deputy Ceremonial Rites Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Taiping Xingguo era, when bandits rose south of the Yangzi, he was made Inspector and promoted to Deputy Ceremonial Rites Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召還，遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: He was recalled and promoted to Ceremonial Rites Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was promoted to Ceremonial Rites Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 監戍兵於威虜軍，塗次鎮州，夜有賊騎扣城門，大呼曰：「官軍至矣。

translations.literal: Supervising garrison troops at Weilu Army, he passed through Zhenzhou on the road; at night bandit horsemen knocked on the city gate and shouted loudly: "The government army has arrived!"
translations.idiomatic: While supervising garrison troops at Weilu Army, he passed through Zhenzhou. At night rebel horsemen knocked on the city gate and shouted, "The imperial army has arrived!"

sentences.zh: 」州將然之，促守吏開關，濟遽止之曰：「此必妄也。

translations.literal: " The prefectural general believed it and urged the gate guards to open the pass; Ji hastily stopped them, saying: "This must be false."
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural commander believed them and ordered the gates opened. Ji stopped them at once. "This must be a ruse," he said.

sentences.zh: 」及旦，果有敵兵遁去。

translations.literal: " By dawn enemy troops had indeed fled away.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn enemy troops were indeed seen fleeing.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之，遷西上閤門使、定州都監，就加行營鈐轄，尋知定州。

translations.literal: Taizong commended him, promoted him to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Chief Supervisor of Dingzhou, and at the same time added Field Headquarters Commissioner; shortly thereafter he was made prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong praised him and made him Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Chief Supervisor of Dingzhou, with additional rank as Field Headquarters Commissioner; he soon became prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹三萬騎來攻，濟逆擊於徐河，斬數千級，獲牛馬、鎧仗甚眾。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand Khitan horsemen came to attack; Ji counterattacked at the Xu River, beheaded several thousand, and captured a great many cattle, horses, and armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: When thirty thousand Khitan horsemen attacked, Ji counterattacked at the Xu River, killed several thousand, and captured large numbers of cattle, horses, arms, and armor.

sentences.zh: 淳化初，與周瑩同判四方館，未幾，為鎮州行營鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chunhua he served together with Zhou Ying as Associate Director of the Four Directions Hall; before long he was made Field Headquarters Commissioner of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chunhua reign he served with Zhou Ying as Associate Director of the Four Directions Hall, and soon became Field Headquarters Commissioner of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 又與李繼隆擊賊於唐河，濟短兵陷陣，賊大敗走，優詔褒美。

translations.literal: He again joined Li Jilong in attacking bandits at the Tang River; Ji with short weapons broke into the enemy line, the bandits were utterly defeated and fled, and a special edict praised and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined Li Jilong in attacking bandits on the Tang River. Ji fought at close quarters in the enemy line, routed the rebels, and received a special edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 初，繼隆以濟性剛，不悅之；

translations.literal: At first Jilong, because Ji was stiff in character, was displeased with him;
translations.idiomatic: At first Li Jilong disliked Ji because of his stubborn temperament;

sentences.zh: 及是役，撫濟恨相知之晚。

translations.literal: after this campaign he stroked Ji and regretted that they had not known each other sooner.
translations.idiomatic: but after this campaign he embraced Ji and regretted that they had not become friends sooner.

sentences.zh: 改四方館使，復知定州，徙天雄軍鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was changed to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall, again made prefect of Dingzhou, and moved to Commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall, again appointed prefect of Dingzhou, and then transferred to Commissioner of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 遷客省使，復知定州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Guest Bureau and again made prefect of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Guest Bureau and again made prefect of Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，改內客省使、知鎮州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao he was changed to Commissioner of the Inner Guest Bureau and made administrator of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhidao he was made Commissioner of the Inner Guest Bureau and administrator of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 立春日，出土牛以祭，酌奠始畢，有卒挾牛去。

translations.literal: On the day of the Beginning of Spring the clay ox was brought out for sacrifice; just as the libation was finished a soldier seized the ox and carried it off.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of spring, when the clay ox was brought out for the rite, a soldier seized it and carried it off just as the libation ended.

sentences.zh: 濟察其舉止，知欲為變，亟命擒之，果有竊發者數十人，已劫鄽間矣，悉蒐捕腰斬之，軍民肅然。

translations.literal: Ji observed his conduct, knew he intended mutiny, and urgently ordered his capture; indeed several tens of men were secretly preparing to rise, had already raided the market quarter, and all were hunted down and cut in two at the waist; army and people were awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: Ji observed the man's conduct, saw that a mutiny was planned, and had him seized at once. Several dozen conspirators who had already raided the market were hunted down and executed by waist-slicing, and order was restored among soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 濟在鎮、定凡十五年，威績甚著。

translations.literal: Ji was in Zhen and Ding for fifteen years in all, and his authority and achievements were very notable.
translations.idiomatic: Ji spent fifteen years in all at Zhen and Ding, where his authority and achievements were conspicuous.

sentences.zh: 召還，知天雄軍。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made administrator of the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made administrator of the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，李繼遷叛，以濟領順州團練使、知靈州兼都部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping Li Jiqian rebelled; Ji was made Militia Commissioner of Shunzhou, administrator of Lingzhou, and concurrently Chief Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping reign, when Li Jiqian rebelled, Ji was made Militia Commissioner of Shunzhou, prefect of Lingzhou, and Chief Commander.

sentences.zh: 至州二年，謀緝八鎮，興屯田之利，民甚賴之。

translations.literal: After two years at the prefecture he planned to pacify the eight garrisons and develop the benefits of military colonies; the people greatly relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years he planned to secure the eight frontier garrisons and develop military colonies, and the people came to rely on him greatly.

sentences.zh: 其年，清遠軍陷，夏人大集，斷餉道，孤軍絕援，濟刺指血染奏，求救甚急，兵不至，城陷，死之。

translations.literal: That year Qingyuan Army fell; the Xia gathered in great force, cut the supply route, and the isolated army was cut off from aid; Ji pricked his finger and stained his memorial with blood, urgently begging rescue; troops did not arrive, the city fell, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qingyuan Army fell. The Tangut forces gathered in strength, cut his supply lines, and left his isolated garrison without relief. Ji pricked his finger and wrote a blood-stained memorial begging urgently for help. No troops came. The city fell, and he died.

sentences.zh: 上聞嗟悼，特贈鎮江軍節度。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it he sighed in grief and specially posthumously granted him Military Commissioner of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard the news he mourned him and posthumously granted him the rank of Military Commissioner of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 三子並優進秩。

translations.literal: All three sons were given preferential advancement in rank.
translations.idiomatic: All three of his sons were given preferential advancement in rank.

sentences.zh: 濟在諸使中甚有聲望，及沒，夏人皆惜之。

translations.literal: Ji had great reputation and standing among the various commissioners; when he died, even the Xia all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Ji enjoyed great standing among the frontier commissioners, and when he died even the Tanguts mourned him.

sentences.zh: 景德中，濟妻永泰郡君景氏卒，特詔追封平陽郡夫人，諸子給奉終喪。

translations.literal: During Jingde Ji's wife, Lady Jing of Yongtai Commandery, died; a special edict posthumously enfeoffed her as Lady of Pingyang Commandery, and the sons were granted stipends through the end of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde reign Ji's wife, Lady Jing of Yongtai Commandery, died. A special edict posthumously enfeoffed her as Lady of Pingyang Commandery, and his sons were granted stipends through the mourning period.

sentences.zh: 子德谷虞部郎中，德基至如京使，德豐殿中丞。

translations.literal: His son Degu became Director of the Works Bureau; Deji rose to Commissioner for the Capital; Defeng became Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Degu became Director of the Works Bureau; Deji rose to Commissioner for the Capital; Defeng became Palace Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 濟兄麗澤、弟麗正，並進士及第。

translations.literal: Ji's elder brother Lize and younger brother Lizheng both passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's elder brother Lize and younger brother Lizheng both passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 麗澤至右補闕，麗正至金部員外郎。

translations.literal: Lize rose to Right Remonstrator; Lizheng rose to Outer Gentleman of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Lize rose to Right Remonstrator; Lizheng rose to Outer Gentleman of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 麗正子德輿，為殿中丞。

translations.literal: Lizheng's son Deyu became Palace Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Lizheng's son Deyu became Palace Secretariat Attendant.

sentences.zh: 李繼宣

translations.literal: Li Jixuan
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixuan

sentences.zh: 李繼宣，開封浚儀人。

translations.literal: Li Jixuan was a native of Junyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jixuan came from Junyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，補右班殿直，令與御帶更直，裁十七歲。

translations.literal: During Qiande he entered service as Right Class Palace Attendant and was ordered to rotate guard duty with the Imperial Belt Guard; he was only seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande reign he entered service as Right Class Palace Attendant and was assigned to rotate guard duty with the Imperial Belt Guard at the age of only seventeen.

sentences.zh: 嘗命往陝州捕虎，殺二十餘，生致二虎、一豹以獻。

translations.literal: He was once ordered to go to Shaanzhou to hunt tigers; he killed more than twenty and presented two tigers and one leopard alive.
translations.idiomatic: He was once sent to Shaanzhou to hunt tigers, killed more than twenty, and presented two live tigers and a leopard to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，掌南作坊使，改供奉官，出為邠、寧、慶三州巡檢、都監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he managed the Southern Workshops Commissioner, was changed to Presentation Officer, and went out as Inspector and Chief Supervisor of the three prefectures of Bin, Ning, and Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo era he managed the Southern Workshops, became Presentation Officer, and was sent out as Inspector and Chief Supervisor of Bin, Ning, and Qing.

sentences.zh: 繼宣本名繼隆，與明德皇后兄同姓名。

translations.literal: Jixuan's original name was Jilong, the same name as the elder brother of Empress Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan's original name was Jilong, the same as that of Empress Mingde's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 至是，太宗為改焉。

translations.literal: At this time Taizong changed it for him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then changed his name.

sentences.zh: 五年，召還，承受定州路奏事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was recalled and received memorials from the Dingzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was recalled to receive memorials from the Dingzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 奉詔修長城口、平塞威虜靜戎軍、保州，又領兵入敵境，獲老幼千餘，牛畜數百。

translations.literal: By imperial order he repaired the Great Wall Pass, Ping Fort, Weilu Army, Jingrong Army, and Baozhou; he also led troops into enemy territory and captured more than a thousand old and young, and several hundred cattle.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he repaired the Great Wall Pass, Ping Fort, Weilu Army, Jingrong Army, and Baozhou. He also led troops into enemy territory and captured more than a thousand civilians and several hundred head of cattle.

sentences.zh: 又率兵捍契丹於乾寧泥姑海口。

translations.literal: He again led troops to resist the Khitan at the mouth of the Nigu River in Qianning.
translations.idiomatic: He again led troops to resist the Khitan at the mouth of the Nigu River in Qianning.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇靜戎軍，從崔彥進過拒馬河接戰，自午至申，大敗之。

translations.literal: When the Khitan attacked Jingrong Army he followed Cui Yanjin across the Juma River to engage them, fighting from the hour wu to the hour shen, and utterly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan attacked Jingrong Army he followed Cui Yanjin across the Juma River and fought from midday to late afternoon, routing them completely.

sentences.zh: 又為貝州監軍。

translations.literal: He again served as supervisory commissioner at Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He again served as army supervisor at Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，曹彬北征，繼宣從先鋒李繼隆至方城，力戰三日，大軍繼至，遂克固州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi Cao Bin campaigned north; Jixuan followed the vanguard Li Jilong to Fangcheng, fought fiercely for three days, the main army arrived in succession, and they thereupon captured Guzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi, during Cao Bin's northern campaign, Jixuan followed the vanguard Li Jilong to Fangcheng and fought fiercely for three days until the main army arrived and Guzhou was taken.

sentences.zh: 進壁涿州東，又與敵鬥，乘勝攻北門，克之。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped east of Zhuozhou, again fought the enemy, and taking advantage of victory attacked the north gate and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and encamped east of Zhuozhou, fought the enemy again, and pressing his advantage stormed and captured the north gate.

sentences.zh: 日領輕騎度涿河，覘敵勢，又將五千騎援米信，因率勁騎追至新城北，大敗之，斬其酋賀恩相公，繼宣亦中流矢。

translations.literal: By day he led light cavalry across the Zhuo River to observe the enemy's strength; he again led five thousand horsemen to reinforce Mi Xin, and thereupon led crack cavalry in pursuit to north of Xincheng, utterly defeating them and beheading their chieftain Chief He'en; Jixuan also took an arrow in the body.
translations.idiomatic: By day he led light cavalry across the Zhuo River to scout the enemy, then took five thousand horsemen to reinforce Mi Xin. He pursued with crack cavalry to north of Xincheng, routed the enemy, and beheaded their chieftain Chief He'en. Jixuan himself was struck by an arrow.

sentences.zh: 大軍還雄州取芻糧，遇契丹新城，疾戰至暮，繼宣中十創，劍及兜鍪。

translations.literal: The main army returned to Xiongzhou to fetch fodder and grain, encountered the Khitan at Xincheng, fought fiercely until evening; Jixuan received ten wounds, and swords reached his helmet.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army returned to Xiongzhou for fodder, it met the Khitan at Xincheng and fought until evening. Jixuan suffered ten wounds, and enemy swords struck his helmet.

sentences.zh: 明日復戰，繼隆為敵所邀，繼宣以所部拔之，且戰且行，奪涿河，數日，乃至涿州。

translations.literal: The next day they fought again; Jilong was intercepted by the enemy; Jixuan with his command rescued him, fighting as they went, seized the Zhuo River, and after several days at last reached Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they fought again. Li Jilong was cut off by the enemy, and Jixuan fought his way through with his own troops, recovered the Zhuo River crossing, and reached Zhuozhou after several days.

sentences.zh: 及棄州保歧溝關，又戰拒馬上，追奔至孤山，契丹乃引去。

translations.literal: When they abandoned the prefecture and held Qigou Pass, they again fought on the Juma River, pursued the fleeing enemy to Gushan, and the Khitan then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the army abandoned Zhuozhou and held Qigou Pass, they fought again on the Juma River, pursued the fleeing Khitan to Gushan, and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 留屯滿城，俄還貝州。

translations.literal: He remained garrisoned at Mancheng, and shortly returned to Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He remained garrisoned at Mancheng, then soon returned to Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 召入，以功超授崇儀使，代王繼恩為易州駐泊都監，賜錢五十萬，白金五百兩。

translations.literal: He was summoned in and, for his merit, was promoted beyond regular rank to Ceremonial Rites Commissioner, replacing Wang Jien as Garrison Chief Supervisor of Yizhou, and was bestowed five hundred thousand cash and five hundred taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, he was promoted out of turn to Ceremonial Rites Commissioner and replaced Wang Jien as Garrison Chief Supervisor of Yizhou. He was rewarded with five hundred thousand cash and five hundred taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 又領騎兵五千戍北平，押大陣東偏，受田重進節度，屯長城口。

translations.literal: He again led five thousand cavalry to garrison Beiping, commanded the eastern wing of the main army, was under the command of Tian Zhongjin, and encamped at the Great Wall Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He again led five thousand cavalry to garrison Beiping, commanded the eastern wing of the main army under Tian Zhongjin, and encamped at the Great Wall Pass.

sentences.zh: 敵至大溝，繼宣進滿城。

translations.literal: When the enemy reached Dagou, Jixuan advanced to Mancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy reached Dagou, Jixuan advanced to Mancheng.

sentences.zh: 敵至定州，奪唐河橋，重進召繼宣洎田紹斌赴援，紹斌為敵所敗，繼宣獨按部轉鬥入定州。

translations.literal: When the enemy reached Dingzhou and seized the Tang River bridge, Zhongjin summoned Jixuan together with Tian Shaobin to go to the rescue; Shaobin was defeated by the enemy, but Jixuan alone led his command in turning battle into Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy reached Dingzhou and seized the Tang River bridge, Tian Zhongjin summoned Jixuan and Tian Shaobin to the rescue. Shaobin was defeated, but Jixuan fought his way alone into Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 敵兵北去，重進命將五千騎躡其後，抵拒馬河。

translations.literal: The enemy troops went north; Zhongjin ordered a general with five thousand horsemen to follow on their heels as far as the Juma River.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy withdrew north, Tian Zhongjin sent a general with five thousand horsemen in pursuit as far as the Juma River.

sentences.zh: 及敵據楊疃，繼宣徑掩擊之，遂焚廬舍而遁。

translations.literal: When the enemy occupied Yangtuan, Jixuan made a direct surprise attack on them, and they thereupon burned their dwellings and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy occupied Yangtuan, Jixuan attacked by surprise and drove them off after they burned their camps.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，為高陽關行營都監。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi he was made Field Headquarters Chief Supervisor of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongxi he was made Field Headquarters Chief Supervisor of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，契丹騎至瀛、鎮，繼宣率步騎萬人入敵境，抵勝務，焚聚落，獲生口，契丹乃引還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong Khitan horsemen reached Ying and Zhen; Jixuan led ten thousand infantry and cavalry into enemy territory, reached Shengwu, burned settlements, captured prisoners, and the Khitan then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong reign, when Khitan horsemen reached Ying and Zhen, Jixuan led ten thousand infantry and cavalry into enemy territory to Shengwu, burned settlements, took prisoners, and the Khitan withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時易州候騎不至，繼宣於易州、平塞軍、長城口、威虜靜戎順安軍至高陽，為望櫓七所，舉烽以候警急。

translations.literal: At the time the scout horsemen of Yizhou did not arrive; Jixuan from Yizhou, Ping Fort, Great Wall Pass, Weilu Army, Jingrong Army, Shun'an Army to Gaoyang built seven watch towers and raised beacon fires to watch for urgent alarms.
translations.idiomatic: When scout horsemen from Yizhou failed to appear, Jixuan built seven watch towers from Yizhou through Ping Fort, the Great Wall Pass, Weilu Army, Jingrong Army, and Shun'an Army to Gaoyang, and lit beacon fires to warn of attack.

sentences.zh: 二年，為鎮、定、高陽關三路排陣都監，押大陣西偏。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made Battle-Array Chief Supervisor of the three routes of Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass, commanding the western wing of the main army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Battle-Array Chief Supervisor of the Zhen, Ding, and Gaoyang Pass routes, commanding the western wing of the main army.

sentences.zh: 與李繼隆部芻糧抵威虜，還度徐河，為敵追襲。

translations.literal: Together with Li Jilong he escorted fodder to Weilu Army, and on the return crossed the Xu River and was pursued by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Jilong he escorted fodder to Weilu Army, and on the return march across the Xu River they were pursued by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 繼宣駐軍與鬥，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Jixuan halted his army and fought, killing and capturing a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan halted and fought, killing and capturing a great many.

sentences.zh: 又領騎二千，敗契丹於保州西射城，追薄西山，有詔褒美。

translations.literal: He again led two thousand horsemen, defeated the Khitan at Shecheng west of Baozhou, pursued close to West Mountain, and received an edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He again led two thousand horsemen, defeated the Khitan at Shecheng west of Baozhou, pursued them to West Mountain, and received an edict of praise.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，徙知保州，又轉莊宅使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua he was transferred to administrator of Baozhou, and again made Commissioner of Imperial Estates.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua he was transferred to administrator of Baozhou and then made Commissioner of Imperial Estates.

sentences.zh: 築關城，浚外濠，葺營舍千五百區；

translations.literal: He built the pass city, dredged the outer moat, and repaired fifteen hundred barracks;
translations.idiomatic: He built the pass city, dredged the outer moat, and repaired fifteen hundred barracks.

sentences.zh: 造船二百艘，入雞距泉以運糧，人咸便之。

translations.literal: built two hundred boats, entered the Jiju Spring to transport grain, and all the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He built two hundred boats and used the Jiju Spring to transport grain, to the great convenience of the people.

sentences.zh: 數月，徙定州行營都監，戍深州，改高陽關行營都監。

translations.literal: Several months later he was moved to Field Headquarters Chief Supervisor of Dingzhou, garrisoned Shenzhou, and changed to Field Headquarters Chief Supervisor of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he became Field Headquarters Chief Supervisor of Dingzhou, garrisoned Shenzhou, and was then made Field Headquarters Chief Supervisor of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 課軍中勁弩，為入陣之備。

translations.literal: He drilled the army in powerful crossbows as preparation for entering battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: He trained the army in powerful crossbows in preparation for battle.

sentences.zh: 五年，領高州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given charge of Gaozhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made prefect of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 會契丹泛海劫千乘縣，繼宣請於海口置砦以禦之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan crossed the sea to raid Qiansheng County; Jixuan requested that a fort be placed at the estuary to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided Qiansheng County by sea, Jixuan asked that a fort be built at the estuary to defend against them.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，遷北作坊使，俄召還，加南作坊使，出為鎮州行營鈐轄。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao he was transferred to Commissioner of the Northern Workshops; shortly he was recalled, given the additional title of Commissioner of the Southern Workshops, and sent out as Field Headquarters Commissioner of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhidao he was made Commissioner of the Northern Workshops, soon recalled and also made Commissioner of the Southern Workshops, then sent out as Field Headquarters Commissioner of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇定州，命主無地分馬。

translations.literal: When the Khitan attacked Dingzhou, he was ordered to command unassigned horses.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan attacked Dingzhou, he was ordered to take command of unassigned cavalry.

sentences.zh: 敵至懷德橋，繼宣領兵三千掩襲之。

translations.literal: When the enemy reached Huaide Bridge, Jixuan led three thousand troops in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy reached Huaide Bridge, Jixuan led three thousand men in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 至則契丹已壞橋，繼宣橫木而度，追奔五十餘里。

translations.literal: When he arrived the Khitan had already destroyed the bridge; Jixuan laid timbers across and crossed, pursuing the fleeing enemy for more than fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived the Khitan had already destroyed the bridge. Jixuan laid timbers across and crossed, then pursued the enemy for more than fifty li.

sentences.zh: 契丹焚鎮州中渡、常山二橋，繼宣領兵趣之，契丹保豐隆山砦，繼宣伐木治常山橋，契丹聞之，大懼，拔砦遁走。

translations.literal: The Khitan burned the two bridges at Zhongdu and Changshan in Zhenzhou; Jixuan led troops to hurry there; the Khitan held the Fenglong Mountain fort; Jixuan felled timber to repair the Changshan bridge; when the Khitan heard of it they were greatly afraid, abandoned the fort, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan burned the Zhongdu and Changshan bridges at Zhenzhou. Jixuan marched to meet them while the Khitan held Fenglong Mountain fort. He felled timber to repair the Changshan bridge, and when the Khitan heard of this they abandoned their fort and fled in alarm.

sentences.zh: 繼宣銳於追襲，傅潛為部署，繼宣詣潛請行，頗為所抑。

translations.literal: Jixuan was keen on pursuit; Fu Qian was Commander; Jixuan went to Qian to request permission to advance and was considerably restrained by him.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan was eager to pursue, but Commander Fu Qian held him back when he asked permission to advance.

sentences.zh: 及召潛屬吏，詔繼宣與高瓊同主軍事，逐敵越拒馬河，復為鎮州鈐轄。

translations.literal: When Qian was summoned with his subordinate officials, an edict ordered Jixuan together with Gao Qiong jointly to direct military affairs, drive the enemy beyond the Juma River, and he again became Commissioner of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Qian was summoned to answer for his conduct, an edict put Jixuan and Gao Qiong jointly in command, ordered them to drive the enemy beyond the Juma River, and restored Jixuan as Commissioner of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 受詔按視緣邊城砦，權知威虜軍，敵騎至城下，屢出兵設伏，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: By imperial order he inspected the frontier forts and stockades, acted as administrator of Weilu Army; when enemy horsemen reached the foot of the city he repeatedly sent out troops to set ambushes and killed and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he inspected the frontier forts and stockades and acted as administrator of Weilu Army. When enemy horsemen reached the walls he repeatedly sent out ambushes and killed or captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 俄還鎮州。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he returned to Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平四年，拜西上閤門使，領康州刺史，為前陣鈐轄，與秦翰、楊延昭、楊嗣分屯靜戎、威虜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianping he was appointed Western Upper Gate Commissioner, given charge of Kangzhou as prefect, made Vanguard Commissioner, and together with Qin Han, Yang Yanzhao, and Yang Si was stationed separately at Jingrong and Weilu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianping he was made Western Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Kangzhou, placed in command of the vanguard, and stationed with Qin Han, Yang Yanzhao, and Yang Si at Jingrong and Weilu.

sentences.zh: 敵至，會師於威虜，延昭、嗣輕騎先赴羊山，繼宣與翰、分左右隊各整所部，翰全軍亦往，繼宣留壁赤虜，止以二騎繼進。

translations.literal: When the enemy arrived they united at Weilu Army; Yanzhao and Si with light cavalry went first to Sheep Mountain; Jixuan and Han divided into left and right teams and each arrayed his command; Han's whole army also went; Jixuan remained to hold Chilu, advancing with only two horsemen in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy arrived the commanders united at Weilu. Yang Yanzhao and Yang Si went ahead with light cavalry to Sheep Mountain. Jixuan and Qin Han divided into left and right wings and arrayed their troops. Qin Han took his whole force forward while Jixuan held Chilu and advanced with only two horsemen following.

sentences.zh: 至，則延昭、嗣適為敵所乘。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Yanzhao and Si happened to be taken advantage of by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Yang Yanzhao and Yang Si were already being overwhelmed by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 繼宣即召赤虜之師，與翰師合勢大戰，敵走上羊山。

translations.literal: Jixuan immediately summoned the troops at Chilu, united strength with Han's army in a great battle, and the enemy fled up Sheep Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan at once summoned the troops from Chilu, joined Qin Han's force, and fought a great battle that drove the enemy up Sheep Mountain.

sentences.zh: 繼宣逐之，環山麓至其陰。

translations.literal: Jixuan pursued them, circling the foot of the mountain to its shaded side.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan pursued them around the foot of the mountain to its northern slope.

sentences.zh: 繼宣馬連中矢斃，凡三易騎，進至牟山谷，大克捷。

translations.literal: Jixuan's horse was struck repeatedly by arrows and died; he changed mounts three times in all, advanced to Mougu Valley, and won a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan's horse was killed by repeated arrow strikes. He changed mounts three times, advanced to Mougu Valley, and won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 延昭、嗣、翰之師，初頓赤虜，既而退保威虜，繼宣以所部獨與敵角，薄暮，始至威虜。

translations.literal: The armies of Yanzhao, Si, and Han at first encamped at Chilu, then withdrew to defend Weilu; Jixuan with his command alone contended with the enemy, and at dusk at last reached Weilu.
translations.idiomatic: The forces of Yang Yanzhao, Yang Si, and Qin Han had first encamped at Chilu, then withdrawn to Weilu. Jixuan fought the enemy alone with his own troops and did not reach Weilu until dusk.

sentences.zh: 詔書稱獎，特加檢校官及食邑。

translations.literal: An edict praised and commended him, specially adding an acting rank and fief households.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended him and specially added an acting rank and households to his fief.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙定州鈐轄，扞契丹於唐河。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Commissioner of Dingzhou and defended against the Khitan on the Tang River.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Commissioner of Dingzhou and defended the Tang River against the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 會緣邊都巡檢使楊延昭、楊嗣禦敵師敗，詔繼宣與內殿崇班王汀代之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Frontier Chief Inspectors Yang Yanzhao and Yang Si were defeated fighting the enemy army; an edict ordered Jixuan and Inner Hall Attendant Wang Ting to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: When Frontier Chief Inspectors Yang Yanzhao and Yang Si were defeated in battle, an edict ordered Jixuan and Inner Hall Attendant Wang Ting to replace them.

sentences.zh: 望都之敗，敵騎剽郡縣，繼宣壁徐河，契丹數十隊薄威虜，威虜魏能與戰，走之，久而繼宣始至。

translations.literal: After the defeat at Wangdu, enemy horsemen raided prefectures and counties; Jixuan fortified at the Xu River; several tens of Khitan bands pressed on Weilu; Wei Neng of Weilu fought them and drove them off; only after a long time did Jixuan arrive.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at Wangdu, enemy horsemen raided the prefectures. Jixuan held the Xu River line while dozens of Khitan columns pressed Weilu. Wei Neng fought them off, but Jixuan arrived only after a long delay.

sentences.zh: 又寇靜戎，汀請分兵自將襲契丹，繼宣拒之，雖日出遊騎偵敵勢，屢徙砦而未嘗出戰。

translations.literal: They again attacked Jingrong; Ting requested to divide the troops and personally lead a raid on the Khitan; Jixuan refused; although each day he sent out scouting horsemen to observe the enemy, he moved stockades repeatedly yet never went out to battle.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy attacked Jingrong again, Wang Ting asked to divide the force and lead a raid himself. Jixuan refused. Though he sent out scouts daily and shifted camps repeatedly, he never gave battle.

sentences.zh: 為能、汀所發，召還，令樞密院問狀，降為如京副使。

translations.literal: Impeached by Neng and Ting, he was recalled, ordered to answer before the Bureau of Military Affairs, and demoted to Deputy Commissioner for the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached by Wei Neng and Wang Ting, he was recalled, questioned by the Bureau of Military Affairs, and demoted to Deputy Commissioner for the Capital.

sentences.zh: 景德初，加如京使、鎮州鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde he was given the additional rank of Commissioner for the Capital and Commissioner of Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde reign he was made Commissioner for the Capital and Commissioner of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹乘秋來攻，時桑贊病足，鄭誠赴定州，繼宣獨主鎮州全師，歷屯邢、趙。

translations.literal: The Khitan took advantage of autumn to attack; at the time Sang Zan was ill in the feet, Zheng Cheng went to Dingzhou, and Jixuan alone directed the entire army of Zhenzhou, encamping in succession at Xing and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan attacked in autumn. Sang Zan was crippled by foot ailment, Zheng Cheng went to Dingzhou, and Jixuan alone commanded the full army of Zhenzhou, shifting camps between Xing and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及與契丹和，命為高陽關鈐轄。

translations.literal: When peace was made with the Khitan, he was ordered to be Commissioner of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made with the Khitan, he was made Commissioner of Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 是冬，復為西上閤門使，領康州刺史。

translations.literal: That winter he again became Western Upper Gate Commissioner and was given charge of Kangzhou as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he again became Western Upper Gate Commissioner and prefect of Kangzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，兼知瀛州。

translations.literal: In the third year he was concurrently made administrator of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was also made administrator of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 繼宣罕識字，上以河間郡事繁，慮獄訟有枉，命高繼勳代之，止為鈐轄。

translations.literal: Jixuan rarely knew written characters; because the affairs of Hejian Commandery were numerous, the emperor feared that lawsuits might be wrongly decided and ordered Gao Jixun to replace him, leaving Jixuan only as Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan could barely read. Fearing miscarriages of justice in the busy Hejian commandery, the emperor replaced him with Gao Jixun and left him only as commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，徙鎮、定兩路鈐轄，進秩東上閤門使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu he was transferred to Commissioner of the Zhen and Ding circuits, and advanced in rank to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era he became Commissioner of the Zhen and Ding circuits and was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召還，改鄆州部署，加四方館使。

translations.literal: He was recalled, changed to Commander of Yanzhou, and given the additional title of Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made Commander of Yanzhou and Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall.

sentences.zh: 以疾，授西京水南都巡檢使，每夕罕巡警，為留司所舉，特詔增巡檢一員，專主夜巡。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was appointed Southern Capital Inspector of the Western Capital Water Office; each evening he rarely made patrol rounds, was reported by the capital resident administration, and a special edict added one inspector devoted solely to night patrol.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he was appointed Southern Capital Inspector of the Western Capital Water Office but rarely patrolled at night. Reported by the capital administration, he received a special edict adding an inspector devoted solely to night rounds.

sentences.zh: 六年，疾甚，求至京師尋醫，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his illness was severe; he requested to come to the capital to seek medical treatment and died, at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his illness worsened. He asked to seek treatment at court and died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 子守忠，左侍禁、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: His son Shouzhong became Left Palace Guard and Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouzhong became Left Palace Guard and Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 張旦，趙州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Dan was a native of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dan came from Zhao Prefecture.
